title: Conversation map: qualify inference opportunities (midmarket play)
content:
Slide 1 — Title: Conversation map: qualify inference opportunities (midmarket)
Speaker note: One-page conversation flow for SDRs/AEs to determine if a prospect is a good fit for Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted API. Not exhaustive — designed for quick use in discovery calls and pre-demo qualification.
---
Slide 2 — Goal & success metrics
Bullets:
- Primary goal: Determine buy-in for production-grade inference (SLA, throughput, data isolation) within first 2 discovery calls.
- Success metrics: conversion to technical discovery >= 40%, demo acceptance rate >= 30%, false-positive qualification <= 15%
Speaker note: These are operational metrics we want field to track; keep it high-level in conversation.
---
Slide 3 — 30-second opener (SDR script)
Script snippets:
- "Hi {name}, quick question: are you building features that must serve heavy user traffic with predictable latency and strict data controls?"
- If yes: "Great — we help teams keep inference costs predictable while meeting latency SLAs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- If no: pivot to pricing/usage interest.
Objection cues: "We'll just use hosted models" -> Probe for 1) traffic growth, 2) data sensitivity, 3) latency pain.
---
Slide 4 — High-level qualifying checklist (use as tick-box on call)
Checklist items (ask verbally, mark Y/N):
1) Expected peak concurrent users or TPS? (estimate)
2) Latency SLO requirements (p50/p95 target)
3) Data residency / compliance constraints (is PHI/PII involved?)
4) Budget model preference (pay-as-you-go vs committed)
5) Need for model customization or on-prem deployment
6) Must-have throughput/embedding volume per month
Note: capture approximate numbers if prospect can't answer exactly.
---
Slide 5 — Decision map (textual, short)
Branch A: Low concurrency, flexible latency, non-sensitive data -> recommend Hosted API pilot.
Branch B: Predictable high throughput OR strict isolation/compliance -> Dedicated or Private (ask about procurement timelines).
Branch C: Needs on-prem/VPC + HSM -> Private deployment (trigger Solutions Eng and Security early).
Speaker note: Use this map to route to correct technical owner and set expectations on procurement lead time.
---
Slide 6 — Signal questions to reveal hidden constraints
Signals and probing follow-ups:
- "Are you seeing variability in response latency or timeouts?" -> shows need for routing and SLA controls.
- "Who will own ops for this feature in production?" -> identifies platform vs product team.
- "What are your monthly embedding volumes or token estimates?" -> helps sizing and pricing.
- "Any legal/regulatory reviewers?" -> brings Legal early.
---
Slide 7 — Mini battlecard: quick counters and positioning (for AE on first call)
Common prospect pushbacks + responses:
- "We can self-host cheaper" -> "Sure, but cost per production token and ops overhead often exceed expectation; we can share a TCO template and a 6–8 week implementation baseline."
- "We need model customization" -> "We support model variants and private model onboarding; we can show previous onboarding timelines and effort estimates."
- "Latency is critical" -> "We provide latency profiles and can propose Dedicated pools with SLO-backed options and failover routes."
---
Slide 8 — Technical discovery trigger checklist (if >=3 Y on qualify checklist)
Trigger items to schedule TE/solutions call:
- Precise throughput numbers or sample traffic profile available
- Explicit data isolation/compliance requirement
- Procurement readiness within 3–6 months
- Interest in dedicated capacity or private deployment
---
Slide 9 — How we frame value (quick elevator pitches)
- Cost predictability: "Reserved Dedicated capacity lets teams forecast unit economics as traffic grows."
- Reliability: "Routing + fallbacks keep customer-facing features online even when models or regions degrade."
- Dev velocity: "Same API across hosted/dedicated/private avoids rewrite when scaling to production."
---
Slide 10 — Ask / close for next step
Suggested ask: "Can we set a 30–45 minute technical discovery with your engineering lead to walk through traffic patterns and sample requests?"
Optional: attach TCO worksheet and a short latency/capacity one-pager post-call.
---
Slide 11 — Field notes template (to paste into CRM after call)
Fields to capture: 1) Primary use case, 2) Estimated peak TPS, 3) Latency SLO, 4) Data sensitivity, 5) Deployment interest (hosted/dedicated/private), 6) Next steps owner, 7) Expected procurement window, 8) Follow-up artifacts sent.
---
